newsitem.title: UK: Shell says China oil refinery plan on hold.
newsitem.headline: Shell says China oil refinery plan on hold.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Friday it was still interested in building a joint venture oil refinery in China but confirmed plans had been put on hold.

Earlier, Chinese sources said proposals for a refinery had been dropped from a plan to build a $6 billion refining and petrochemical complex in the southern Guandong province which has been on the drawing board since the late 1980s.
"The proposal has undergone a number of revisions. We will be concentrating on the petrochemical side with the refinery deferred to a later date," said a Shell spokesman in London.
He said Shell was still awaiting Chinese government approval for the petrochemical plant.
"The refinery will come in later," he said, but declined comment on any new timing for the refinery.

Shell was hoping to build a 160,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) refinery in Huizhou to take advantage of surging Chinese demand for refined oil products, which is expected to grow by nearly six percent a year to 5.3 million bpd by 2005.
Chinese sources said the proposed capacity of the ethylene plant had been increased to 600,000 tonnes from the initial 450,000 tonnes.
Under the original plan, Shell would own 50 percent of the project and Chine Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) 20 percent.
Guangdong provincial government, China Merchant Holding Co and state refiner SINOPEC would each hold 10 percent.
